page: Microsoft Azure EC4es_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon TDX cores with 2 threads per core, operating at clock speeds up to 4.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor features advanced instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AMX tile and int8 execution, alongside a 260 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 32.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, relying instead on network-attached Premium Storage capabilities, and includes zero dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-thread execution alongside expected constraints in multi-core throughput due to its 2-core / 4-thread count. In Geekbench testing, the instance achieved a strong single-core score of 2029.0, backed by an average stress-ng single-core result of 1914.19 and an average PassMark CPU score of 7271.8. However, parallel execution metrics reflect lower raw compute capacity, with multi-core stress-ng at 3931.09 and Geekbench compiling at 4898.0 falling into lower benchmark quartiles. Memory operations register intermediate throughput, with PassMark memory scoring 2131.36 and PassMark database operations at 2752.28, while Redis SET operations reached 5.19 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the EC4es_v6 prioritizes memory density over multi-threaded parallel throughput. The absence of bundled local storage necessitates external volume provisioning for data persistence, while the high 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides significant headroom for footprint-heavy services without paying for excess compute cores. This profile is suited for memory-intensive workloads that require solid single-core responsiveness rather than heavy parallel computation, such as in-memory caching layers, medium-scale relational databases, enterprise applications, and ETL pipeline staging.
